title: Water Damage Restoration in Alexandria, VA

children.text: Water damage doesn’t wait, and in Alexandria, the older housing stock, basements, and Potomac-adjacent neighborhoods mean it happens more often than people expect.
Burst pipes

in winter, sump pump failures during summer storms, washing machine overflows, and sewer backups — when water gets in, the clock starts. Water Damage Pro provides 24/7 emergency water damage restoration across Alexandria, VA, from Old Town and Del Ray to the West End and surrounding neighborhoods.
What we do when you call
Emergency response.

We answer around the clock and dispatch to Alexandria homes and businesses quickly. The first job is always the same: stop the source of water if it isn’t already stopped, and start removing standing water.
Water extraction.
We use professional-grade extraction equipment to remove standing water fast. Speed here matters — the longer water sits, the further it wicks into walls, subfloors, and cabinetry.
Structural drying.

Removing visible water is only half the job. We place commercial air movers and dehumidifiers strategically and monitor moisture levels with meters until walls, floors, and framing read dry. This is what prevents the hidden moisture problems that show up months later.
Mold prevention and remediation.
Mold

can begin growing within 24–48 hours of water exposure. Proper drying usually prevents it, but where growth has already started, we contain and remediate it so it doesn’t spread through the HVAC system or wall cavities.
Insurance coordination.
We document the damage thoroughly and work directly with your insurance company to help your claim move forward.
Common water damage problems in Alexandria homes

Alexandria’s housing mix — historic rowhouses in Old Town, mid-century homes in Del Ray and Rosemont, and newer builds in the West End — each comes with its own risk profile. Frozen and burst pipes are a leading cause of winter claims. Summer thunderstorms overwhelm sump pumps and drainage, flooding basements. Aging supply lines and water heaters fail without warning. And in lower-lying areas near the Potomac, heavy rain events can push water where it doesn’t belong.
Whatever the cause, the response is the same: extract, dry, verify. We don’t leave until moisture readings confirm the structure is actually dry, not just dry to the touch.
What to do in the first hour
If it’s safe, shut off the water at the main valve and turn off electricity to affected areas.
Move valuables, electronics, and furniture out of the water’s path.
Don’t use a household vacuum on standing water, and don’t enter rooms with sagging ceilings.
Call us. The earlier extraction and drying begin, the less damage spreads — and the simpler the restoration.
Why drying matters more than it looks

Most of the cost in a water damage claim isn’t the initial cleanup — it’s the secondary damage: warped floors, swollen drywall, and mold remediation that could have been prevented with proper drying. Industrial dehumidifiers and monitored drying are the difference between a clean restoration and a problem that comes back.
